_readme: Hand-maintained. `stories` sets which clips a story is tested on ('*' = all). `criteria` records, per numbered criterion, the test ids that prove it, its status (PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, N/A, BLOCKED, AGENT-REVIEW-ONLY), a note, and optionally a narrower clip list. A criterion with no status here is FAIL (no test yet), or BLOCKED if none of its clips is available. Regenerate docs/TRACEABILITY.md with: node --import tsx scripts/gen-traceability.mts

clip-G1.note: handoff/reference/G1, with oracle and two reference outputs

clip-G2.what: Talking head with lower thirds and a music bed, 1080p, 3 min

clip-G3.what: Product demo inside a phone mockup, scrolling UI, 60 fps

clip-G4.what: Kinetic typography, per-word animation, motion blur

clip-G5.what: Live action with signs, a hand passing over a title, handheld camera

clip-G6.what: Portrait phone recording, variable frame rate, rotation metadata

clip-G8.what: Hindi source to English, and English to Arabic

clip-G9.what: Two-person interview, both on camera, music bed, 1080p, about 3 min

clip-G10.what: Handheld street vlog with signs and a title over the footage, 4K30

clip-G11.what: 30 s ad with kinetic type, voiceover, music and effects, 1080p60

clip-G12.what: Screen-recorded tutorial with cursor and scrolling, 1440p, about 5 min

clip-G13.what: Music video excerpt with sung lyrics and burned-in lyric captions

clip-G14.what: Hard cases: face profiles, hand over mouth, low light, motion blur

clip-G15.what: Synthetic suite generated by code with exact ground truth
clip-G15.note: generated by the harness (services/video-worker/harness/synth); never hand-labelled

tests: vt K4: a render reports which segments were re-encoded, and only the edited block’s segment is
K4.1.note: Proven by segment hashes on clip-G15 in the worker, through the API, and from the real UI (1 of 3 segments re-encoded). Not yet run on clip-G1.

L1.1.note: Container facts equal on clip-G1. Bitstream SAR and rotation are not yet checked.

L1.2.note: H.264 only so far; HEVC and ProRes are not offered yet.

L2.1.note: Passes on clip-G1 and clip-G15 for the deterministic stages, with wording supplied by the test. Other clips are not sourced, and a full run with the real agent needs the API key.

M4.1.note: Passes on clip-G1 and clip-G15 for the deterministic stages, with wording supplied by the test. Other clips are not sourced, and a full run with the real agent needs the API key.

M4.2.note: The harness and the worker report similarity outside the mask only. The UI's QA report has not been checked for this yet.

W7.2.note: Thumbnail size is enforced by the worker. Lazy loading in the UI is not yet tested.

tests: J3: the timeline shows only translated captions until asked, and each bar ends when its caption leaves the screen
J3.1.note: One bar per caption with its real on-screen span, in a mocked-API browser test and by eye on the real stack. No audio track yet (no voice phase).

tests: J4: typing a translation saves it within two seconds and reports whether it fits
J3.3.note: Selection is shared between timeline, picture and panel; pending and warning colours are shown. 'Needs review' colour is not implemented.

tests: J4: typing a translation saves it within two seconds and reports whether it fits
J4.1.note: Text, size (within 10 %), weight, colour and line breaks edit live against the worker. Font family, alignment and effects cannot be changed yet.

tests: vt J4/J8/K8: an edit is applied, logged with what, where and by whom, and undo and redo replay it
J4.2.note: 'Reset to AI suggestion' works. 'Match source style' exists only as colour/weight 'Match the source'.

tests: J5/J6: the animation is read out in words and numbers; shifting the start warns and "Snap to source" clears it
J5.1.note: Motion is read out in words and numbers with 'Match source'. There is no keyframe or easing editor, and the UI says so.

tests: J5/J6: the animation is read out in words and numbers; shifting the start warns and "Snap to source" clears it
J6.1.note: In and out move by frame steppers with a snap back to source timing. Bars are not draggable and there is no snapping to cuts or pans.

tests: vt J4/J8/K8: an edit is applied, logged with what, where and by whom, and undo and redo replay it
J6.2.note: A departure of one frame or more is stated by the worker, the API and the panel. Proven with the replay doubles and on the synthetic clip (clip-G15) with the real stack; not yet run on clip-G1.

tests: J7: arrow keys move the selected caption one pixel, Shift ten, sent as one change; a drag moves it too
J7.1.note: Drag and 1 px / 10 px nudges work. There are no resize handles; size is changed in the panel.

tests: vt J4/J8/K8: an edit is applied, logged with what, where and by whom, and undo and redo replay it
J8/K8: undo and redo work from the top bar, and the history lists every change with a revert of its own
J8.1.note: Undo and redo cover every edit, AI edits included, and survive a reload (the log is stored). Proven with the replay doubles and on the synthetic clip (clip-G15) with the real stack; not yet run on clip-G1.

tests: vt K1/K3/W5: an instruction becomes a proposal with a picture and an explanation; nothing changes until it is accepted
K1/K2: an area drawn on the picture or a stretch of the timeline becomes the scope; a proposal can be rejected or refined
K1.1.note: A drawn box or a clicked caption plus a typed instruction works, including one run with the real model on the synthetic clip. Proven with the replay doubles and on the synthetic clip (clip-G15) with the real stack; not yet run on clip-G1.

tests: K1/K2: an area drawn on the picture or a stretch of the timeline becomes the scope; a proposal can be rejected or refined
K2.1.note: A stretch of the timeline can be the scope. Only tested against the mocked API and replay doubles.

tests: vt K1/K3/W5: an instruction becomes a proposal with a picture and an explanation; nothing changes until it is accepted
K3.1.note: The proposal has a before/after still and a one-sentence explanation; with the real model it arrived in 11 s on the synthetic clip. No difference view inside the card.

tests: vt K3/K5: a proposal can be rejected or refined, and an ambiguous instruction comes back as one question
K1/K3/W5: tell the AI what to change on the selected caption; the proposal shows a picture, a reason and its steps; Accept applies it
K3.2.note: Accept, Reject and Refine work. Proven with the replay doubles and on the synthetic clip (clip-G15) with the real stack; not yet run on clip-G1.

tests: K4: Re-render batches the pending changes and says which segments were re-encoded
K4.2.note: Measured 1.5 to 1.9 s on the 6-second synthetic clip. Not measured on a 2-minute 1080p video, which is what the criterion asks.

tests: vt K3/K5: a proposal can be rejected or refined, and an ambiguous instruction comes back as one question
K5: an ambiguous instruction comes back as one question with a recommended answer
K5.1.note: One question with two or three options and a recommended one, with replay doubles; the real model has not been seen to ask yet.

tests: vt J4/J8/K8: an edit is applied, logged with what, where and by whom, and undo and redo replay it
J8/K8: undo and redo work from the top bar, and the history lists every change with a revert of its own
K8.1.note: Every change is logged with what, where, why and by whom, each revertible on its own. Entries are numbered per version; there are no separately numbered saved versions yet.

tests: vt K1/K3/W5: an instruction becomes a proposal with a picture and an explanation; nothing changes until it is accepted
W5.1.note: Each instruction has its own thread in the job's trace (looked at, thought, preview, result), shown in the proposal card. The render and check that follow an accept are not part of the thread yet.

I1.1.note: Phrase starts and ends are refined on the audio to within 40 ms on synthetic speech. Word error rate needs a real transcription and labelled clips. No real ElevenLabs call has been made (no key is configured), so nothing here is proven on real speech.

tests: vt voice: phrases are cut at speaker changes, pauses and sentence ends
I1.2.note: Speakers from the provider's diarization are carried on every phrase and each can be given a voice. The transcript cannot be edited before translation yet. No real ElevenLabs call has been made (no key is configured), so nothing here is proven on real speech.

I1.3.note: The agent is told to correct names from on-screen text; whether it does is unproven without a real run. No real ElevenLabs call has been made (no key is configured), so nothing here is proven on real speech.

I2.1.note: Separation is a spectral soft mask with a keep / room tone / silence decision, proven on synthetic voice-over-music and narration. Real run: clip-G1 only (narration, nothing kept). No real clip with music has been dubbed.

I2.2.note: Residual source voice is at or under -30 dB on the synthetic voice-over-music mix (measured against the true voice) and is checked in qa_suite. On the real clip-G1 dub nothing of the source track is kept, so none remains; the first real dub measured -20.5 dB and the owner heard it. Not yet measured on a real clip that has music.

I2.3.note: The agent is told to skip separation on clean narration; unproven without a real run. With no separation the dub replaces the whole track and gaps are digital silence.

I3.1.note: Largest onset error on the real clip-G1 dub: 25 ms over 9 phrases (limit 40), after overlapping source phrases were merged into one unit. One clip, one language.

I3.2.note: Speed is held to 0.90 to 1.10 and a phrase that still does not fit is reported with advice to reword; the harness reproduces the reference's S7d shortfall. Rewording by the agent is unproven without a real run.

I3.3.note: Depends on how the agent writes the phrases; unproven without a real run.

tests: vt voice replay: a voiceover job separates, transcribes, picks a voice, dubs
I4.1.note: On-screen blocks and numerals are offered as anchors with the second each appears, and the agent names the mention. Unproven on a real run.

I4.2.note: Mention timing is estimated from its place in the phrase, then replaced by the word time heard in back-transcription. Both the product check and the harness reproduction of S5 need word timings from a real transcription. No real ElevenLabs call has been made (no key is configured), so nothing here is proven on real speech.

tests: upload: with a key, Voiceover can be switched on, a voice chosen from the library
I5.1.note: Library voices with gender, age, accent and use, search, filter and the provider's sample clip. The sample is not a line from the user's script, and there are no pace tags. Browser test runs against a scripted API.

I5.2.note: Not built: the default voice is the person's default for the language or the agent's choice, not matched to the speaker's pitch and pace.

I5.3.note: No real ElevenLabs call has been made (no key is configured), so nothing here is proven on real speech.

I6.1.note: Voice cloning is not offered at all, so nothing can be cloned without consent. The consent record flow is not built.

I6.2.note: Not built: there is no cloning.

I7.1.note: Per-phrase and whole-track loudness pass together on synthetic mixes and on the real clip-G1 dub (every phrase within 0.4 LU, track -21.4 against -21.8 LUFS). One clip.

I7.2.note: True peak limited to -1 dBTP and 8 ms fades, proven on synthetic phrases; the harness measures the reference dub.

I8.1.note: The agent writes a spoken form (numbers in words, acronyms letter by letter, respelled names) beside the written form. There is no stored pronunciation dictionary. Unproven without a real run.

tests: vt voice: a key term is heard whatever script or spelling it comes back in, and a missing one is still missing
I8.2.note: Key terms are matched across scripts, spellings and number words, and a missing term still fails. Real clip-G1 dub: 9 of 9 heard through a real ElevenLabs transcription. One clip, Hindi only.

tests: export: a dubbed version offers the dubbed voice, the original with the dub as a second track, or the original audio only
I9.1.note: Keep original, replace the voice and add the dub as a second track are built. Captions-only is not.

I9.2.note: In second-track mode the original track's packets are identical to the source (synthetic clip); the on-screen-only export keeps them identical on clip-G1.

V7.1.note: Order built: reword (the agent), then rate within 0.90 to 1.10. Using the speaker's own pauses and borrowing silence are not built.

V7.3.note: A phrase never overlaps the next: one that would is faded out before it and reported as cut short, which can cut a word. The duration check then fails, so it is not silent.

L2.2.note: Dubbed audio is padded or trimmed to the source track's length and checked within one audio frame on a synthetic clip; the harness measures the clip-G1 reference dub. A/V drift over a long file is not measured.

V5.2.note: Each speaker's pitch is measured and the agent chooses a library voice by it (clip-G1: 265 Hz, a female voice chosen without asking). Proven for one speaker; no multi-speaker clip is sourced.
